description: Unique identifier for one simulated subject. Format SSPK-NNNNNN; stable join key used across every table in this delivery.
One of acetaminophen, scopolamine, zolpidem.
GROUND (baseline) or FLIGHT (in-flight microgravity perturbation applied). Zolpidem and the scopolamine PATCH route have no FLIGHT arm - see Scope of the model.
ORAL or PATCH (transdermal). PATCH exists only for scopolamine (GROUND only, no in-flight patch calibration data exists). Acetaminophen and zolpidem are ORAL only.

For ORAL subjects: the single oral dose administered (650 mg acetaminophen; 0.4 mg scopolamine; 10 mg zolpidem - standard single therapeutic doses). For PATCH subjects: the TOTAL dose delivered over the full patch-wear period (1.0 mg over 72 hours, matching the FDA Transderm Scop label), not a per-hour rate.

This subject's body weight. Acetaminophen and scopolamine subjects: individually drawn from a published adult weight distribution (mean ~75kg, not a flat value - see the Data Passport's covariate section). Zolpidem subjects: standardised flat 70kg for every subject (disclosed scope limitation - no weight covariate for zolpidem, see Scope of the model).

This subject's age. Populated (drawn from a published adult age distribution) for acetaminophen subjects only, where the source population-PK model includes an age covariate. NULL for scopolamine and zolpidem subjects (disclosed - no age covariate exists in those drugs' source models).

This subject's TRUE (noise-free) absorption rate constant, after between-subject variability, any covariate effects, and (for FLIGHT subjects) the microgravity perturbation factor have all been applied. NULL for PATCH-route subjects (a patch has no absorption-rate constant - it delivers at a constant zero-order rate; see route).

This subject's TRUE absolute oral bioavailability (0 to 1). NULL for PATCH-route subjects (bioavailability is not a meaningful parameter for a route modelled as direct zero-order delivery into the central compartment; see the Data Passport's Honest Limitations section).
This subject's TRUE systemic clearance, including any covariate effects (age/sex/weight/renal-function, where that drug's source model includes them).
This subject's TRUE central-compartment volume of distribution.
This subject's TRUE intercompartmental clearance between the central and peripheral compartment.
This subject's TRUE peripheral-compartment volume of distribution.
The microgravity perturbation factor actually applied to ka for this subject (1.0 for every GROUND subject by construction; NULL for PATCH subjects, which have no ka).
The microgravity perturbation factor actually applied to bioavailability for this subject (1.0 for every GROUND subject by construction; NULL for PATCH subjects, which have no F).
The microgravity perturbation factor actually applied to clearance for this subject (1.0 for every GROUND subject by construction).

Which real published in-flight human study this subject's perturbation triple was resampled from (acetaminophen FLIGHT subjects only; see the Data Passport for the four source studies). N/A_GROUND for every GROUND subject; N/A_NO_FLIGHT_DATA_FOR_ZOLPIDEM for every zolpidem subject (no flight arm exists for this drug); N/A_NO_FLIGHT_DATA_FOR_PATCH for every scopolamine PATCH subject (no in-flight patch comparison exists in the published literature).

For acetaminophen FLIGHT subjects only: which mission-duration literature cluster this subject's perturbation was drawn from - short_duration_shuttle (Cintron 1987a, short Shuttle missions) or long_duration_station (Kovachevich 2009 + Polyakov 2021, long-duration station missions). N/A_GROUND for every GROUND subject across all three drugs.

This subject's TRUE (noise-free) maximum plasma concentration over the observation window used for this subject's route (24h for ORAL, 96h for PATCH - see the Data Passport).
This subject's TRUE time of maximum plasma concentration.
This subject's TRUE area under the concentration-time curve, extrapolated to infinity.
This subject's TRUE terminal (log-linear) elimination rate constant.
This subject's TRUE terminal elimination half-life (ln 2 / lambda_z_true).

Nominal blood-draw time. Twelve points per subject, on one of two fixed route-specific sampling schedules (0.25-24h for ORAL subjects; 2-96h for PATCH subjects, matching the longer patch-wear/decay window) - see the Data Passport.

Simulated "observed" plasma concentration at this sample time: the TRUE concentration at that time, with drug-appropriate proportional assay noise added and clipped at zero. This column is never bit-identical to any truth_pk_metrics or truth_pk_parameters value - see the Validation Report's leakage-separation checks.

Lower bound of the 2.5th-97.5th percentile reference interval for Cmax_true, computed from this drug AND ROUTE's own GROUND-arm subjects in this dataset (computed per drug+route, not drug alone, so the scopolamine ORAL and PATCH routes - which have very different absolute concentration scales - each get their own, comparable reference band).
Upper bound of the same Cmax reference interval.
Lower bound of the 2.5th-97.5th percentile reference interval for AUC_true, computed per drug+route (see cmax_reference_lo).
Upper bound of the same AUC reference interval.
This subject's Cmax_true divided by the midpoint of its drug+route's reference interval.
This subject's AUC_true divided by the midpoint of its drug+route's reference interval.

BELOW_REFERENCE_RANGE, WITHIN_REFERENCE_RANGE, or ABOVE_REFERENCE_RANGE for Cmax_true against this drug+route's own GROUND-arm reference interval. This is a descriptive comparison against this cohort's own baseline, not a clinical safety or toxicity classification - see Scope of the model.
Same three-way classification for AUC_true.
Join key - see subjects.subject_id. Every zolpidem subject has exactly one row here (zolpidem is the only drug in this dataset with a multi-dose steady-state table).
Number of nightly doses simulated to reach this subject's steady state (7 nightly doses).
The nightly dosing interval used (24 hours).
This subject's TRUE peak plasma concentration within the final (steady-state) dosing interval.
This subject's TRUE trough plasma concentration at the end of the final dosing interval (immediately before the next nightly dose).
This subject's TRUE area under the curve over one full dosing interval (tau) at steady state.
This subject's steady-state AUC_tau divided by their single-dose AUC_true (from truth_pk_metrics) - the actual simulated accumulation after repeated nightly dosing.

The theoretical accumulation ratio for a linear one-compartment-equivalent system, 1/(1-exp(-lambda_z*tau)), computed from this subject's own lambda_z_true and the 24h dosing interval - included so the observed ratio above can be checked against the closed-form prediction (see the Validation Report).
